chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Surely Allah commands you to render trusts to their أهل, and when you judge between الناس, that you judge with justice.

He said: 'It means us, that the first should hand over to the Imam after him the books, the knowledge, and the weapons; and when you judge between the people, that you judge with the justice that is in your hands.'

Then He said to the people: 'O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you.' It means us specifically; He commanded all the believers, up to the Day of qiyamah, to obey us.

Then if you fear a dispute regarding a matter, refer it to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to those vested with authority among you—thus it was revealed. And how could Allah, Mighty and Majestic, command them to obey the possessors of authority and yet permit disputing with them?
Rather, that was said to those who were commanded, those to whom it was said: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you.'

key_terms.أُولِي الْأَمْرِ: those vested with authority, interpreted here as the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: the weaponry transmitted as part of the signs of Imamate
key_terms.الْأَمَانَاتِ: the entrusted matters to be delivered to their rightful أهل
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely designated leader who succeeds the previous Imam
key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: the special divinely guided knowledge entrusted to the Imam
key_terms.الْكُتُبَ: the inherited scriptures or written sources passed on in the line of authority
key_terms.بِالْعَدْلِ: with justice in judgment and authority
key_terms.طَاعَتِنَا: obedience to us, referring to the obedience due to the Imams عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith interpret the verses about trusts and obeying those in authority in Surah al-Nisa?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse of trusts as referring to the transmission of the books, knowledge, and weaponry from one Imam to the next. It also interprets obedience to those vested with authority as a specific command concerning the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, presenting their authority as continuous for the believers until the Day of qiyamah.
